title: skilldrop loop
$comment: RFC-0028. A loop sequences existing skills; it never contains one. Skills stay in flat skills/<name> folders and stay independently installable — a loop is a named order plus the gates between stages. Enforced by validate.py with hand-rolled stdlib checks: skilldrop ships zero runtime dependencies and this file must not become a reason to add `jsonschema`.

name.description: Kebab-case. Must equal the folder name and the LOOP.md frontmatter name — the same triple-match skills are held to.

description.description: Use-case-first. First half says what the loop delivers; second half states the trigger phrases an agent matches on.

kind.description: `loop` advances stage to stage toward a terminal. `wrapper` wraps an arbitrary generator skill chosen at run time — its stages are the passes either side of that generator.

cap.description: Maximum revision rounds before the loop stops looping and emits its conditional or blocked terminal. Default 3, matching agent-loop-design's revision cap.

type.description: The three state types agent-loop-design mandates: 'Every loop has exactly these three state types.'

intent.description: One line: what this stage is for.

skills.description: Skill folder names, in order. Each must be a real skills/<name>. `*` means any generator, and is legal only in a wrapper.

id.description: Named gate, unique across the repo. A gate is a place a human or a script can point at.

kind.description: mechanical = a script's exit code decides. review = a skill or subagent panel decides. human = a person decides and the agent may not proceed without it.

script.description: Repo-relative path to the deciding script. Required when kind is mechanical, forbidden otherwise.

verdicts.description: Every verdict this gate can emit. All must exist in contracts/terminals.json. Must include >=1 pass-class and >=1 non-pass.

revise_to.description: Stage id a revise-class verdict returns to. Must be an earlier stage in this loop.
